editorNote: Today's edition centers on leadership upheaval at Alphabet, where chief scientist Jeff Dean's departure and a DeepMind reshuffle knocked shares down more than 4%. Duolingo's Q2 beat couldn't outrun cautious guidance, Alibaba moved to start charging large users of its next Qwen model, and gold and bitcoin diverged — gold rallying on rate-cut bets while bitcoin's price stalled despite heavy ETF and whale buying.

stories.headline: Alphabet's chief scientist Jeff Dean exits after 27 years as DeepMind reshuffles leadership
stories.summary: Jeff Dean and senior fellow Sanjay Ghemawat are leaving Google to launch AI-for-science venture Discovery Loop, a public benefit corporation with Google as a founding investor. In the same announcement, Demis Hassabis stepped back from day-to-day operational leadership of Google DeepMind to become its chairman and Alphabet's chief scientist, while Koray Kavukcuoglu was promoted to lead the DeepMind unit, reporting directly to CEO Sundar Pichai.
stories.whyItMatters: Alphabet shares fell more than 4% on the August 5 announcement, reflecting investor unease about a leadership shakeup atop the company's AI unit as it races to ship Gemini 4.

sourceLinks.title: Google reveals big shakeup in its AI teams as Jeff Dean leaves and Demis Hassabis moves upstairs

stories.headline: Duolingo tops Q2 revenue and profit estimates, but shares slide on cautious guidance
stories.summary: Duolingo reported Q2 2026 revenue of $298.5 million, up 18.3% year-over-year and 0.9% ahead of estimates, with GAAP EPS of $0.66 beating consensus by 8.9% and adjusted EBITDA of $77.3 million beating estimates by 8%. Next-quarter revenue guidance of $302 million came in 0.9% below analyst expectations, even as full-year revenue guidance was lifted to a $1.21 billion midpoint.
stories.whyItMatters: Shares fell as much as 12% before closing down 9.46% at $122.52 on 3.3x average volume, extending pressure on the stock after Bank of America's downgrade earlier in the week.

stories.headline: Alibaba to charge large enterprise users of its next Qwen AI model, Reuters reports
stories.summary: Two sources told Reuters that Alibaba plans to require major commercial users of its upcoming Qwen3.8-Max open-source model — those building "Model-as-a-Service" offerings generating over $20 million a year — to share a cut of that revenue, mirroring a policy Chinese rival Moonshot AI already applies to its Kimi K3 model. The exact revenue-share percentage is still under negotiation; Moonshot's comparable terms reportedly demand up to 30%.
stories.whyItMatters: The shift marks Alibaba's first departure from offering Qwen models free to enterprise users on their own infrastructure, signaling Chinese AI labs are moving to monetize previously free open-weight models.

sourceLinks.title: Exclusive-Alibaba plans to charge big users of its next open-source AI model, sources say

stories.headline: Gold rallies to $4,254, on pace for its best week since January
stories.summary: Spot gold traded around $4,254 an ounce, up roughly 5% this week, as falling oil prices, a weaker dollar and declining Treasury yields lifted the metal. Traders are watching Friday's non-farm payrolls report, with soft ADP private-sector data — 44,000 jobs added — fueling bets that a weak print could push yields, and gold, further.
stories.whyItMatters: The rally marks gold's best week since January, extending gains as investors position for weaker Fed policy support following soft labor-market data.

sourceLinks.title: Gold Price Forecast Today: XAU/USD Holds Above $4,250 as NFP Takes Center Stage

stories.headline: Bitcoin whales add $1.2 billion in BTC as spot ETFs post their best week since April
stories.summary: Wallets holding 10 to 10,000 BTC accumulated more than 20,000 bitcoin worth about $1.2 billion since July 29, even as the price traded in a narrow band below $65,000. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in $754.69 million over the week, their strongest showing since April.
stories.whyItMatters: The divergence between strong institutional buying and a stalled price highlights how thin conviction remains after the Senate delayed a vote on the CLARITY Act until September.

sourceLinks.title: Bitcoin whales load up on $1.2 billion in BTC as ETFs attract $750 million
